translations.answer: The original poster first pointed out that the input quaternions were not normalized. The questioner then switched to constructing unit quaternions using precise sin/cos values, reducing the matrix difference norm from approximately 0.00075 to 5.16e-14. Therefore, such analyses should first verify the unit norm of the quaternions and preserve sufficient precision before discussing the algorithm or reference frame. The thread does not support the stronger conclusion that 'the zero position and unit attitude must always be used.'
translations.applicability: Applicable to input and dynamics comparison of Pinocchio JointModelFreeFlyer configuration; specific version not indicated.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The questioner reconstructs two sets of quaternions using precise sin(pi/2) and cos(pi/2) and re-calculates them.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Check the norm of the quaternion in the configuration vector before evaluating the algorithm or coordinate system error; use strict normalization for repeated identical matrix comparisons.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Ensure that the quaternion input to JointModelFreeFlyer is normalized; do not directly compare dynamics quantities using low-precision truncated quaternions.
translations.details.environments.0: Pinocchio Python API；JointModelFreeFlyer；Original post provides two-link URDF and full comparison script；specific Pinocchio/OS version not mentioned.
translations.details.limits.0: The thread has not been closed, and the residual of 5.16e-14 has no further explanation; the original author's question regarding whether the position/units pose must be fixed to zero has not been addressed.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Normalized difference norm reduced to 5.16e-14; confirmator confirms significant improvement.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: When the base pose changes during floating base control, the computeCoriolisMatrix function shows discrepancies. How to eliminate the pseudo-error caused by invalid input quaternions?
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The initial quaternion was obtained from Gazebo with two decimal places, and the unit norm was not satisfied.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The Coriolis matrix shows significant differences under different positions and postures. The matrix difference norm for the initial example is 0.00075.

translations.source.title: Unnormalized Floating-Point Quaternions Cause Pseudo-Differences in Pose Using the Pinocchio KineMatics Matrix
translations.title: Why Should We Check for Quaternion Normalization Before Observing Abnormalities in the Floating Base Matrix When the Matrix Seems to Change Anomalyously with Position or Orientation?
